title: Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment
summary: A clinician-facing framework for a multidimensional assessment of an older person living with frailty, integrating medical, functional, cognitive, psychological, social and environmental needs into a coordinated plan.

items.title: What CGA is
mustConfirmOrExclude: A multidimensional, interdisciplinary assessment and management process.
A method for identifying medical, functional, psychological, social and environmental needs.
A coordinated plan with clear goals, responsibilities, review and escalation arrangements.
items.importantLimitation: CGA is a process, not a single score. It cannot be replaced by the Clinical Frailty Scale, a checklist or one consultation.

items.title: When to initiate or refer
mustConfirmOrExclude: Moderate or severe frailty, recurrent falls, delirium, functional decline, multimorbidity, treatment burden, recurrent admission or care breakdown.
Uncertainty about goals, capacity, rehabilitation potential, living arrangements or medication burden.
A need for coordinated input across medical, nursing, pharmacy, therapy and social-care services.

sections.title: History prompts
sections.intro: Build a multidimensional account of current problems, baseline function, supports and what matters to the person.

items.title: Medical
mustConfirmOrExclude: Active acute illness and unresolved symptoms.
Long-term conditions, prognosis and interactions between conditions.
Pain, nutrition, hydration, continence, vision, hearing, oral health and skin integrity.
Medication reconciliation, adherence, benefit, harm and treatment burden.

items.title: Functional
mustConfirmOrExclude: Baseline and current mobility, transfers, gait, balance and falls.
Personal activities of daily living: washing, dressing, toileting, feeding and continence.
Instrumental activities: shopping, cooking, finances, transport and medicines.
Rehabilitation potential, equipment and environmental barriers.

items.title: Cognition and psychological health
mustConfirmOrExclude: Delirium and acute change.
Dementia or chronic cognitive impairment.
Mood, anxiety, sleep, behaviour and loneliness.
Capacity for relevant decisions and communication needs.

items.title: Social and environmental
mustConfirmOrExclude: Living arrangement, carers, formal support and carer strain.
Home safety, heating, food, phone access, transport and safeguarding.
Community services, social connection and ability to attend appointments.

items.title: What matters most
mustConfirmOrExclude: The person’s priorities, acceptable trade-offs and outcomes they value.
Advance care plan, treatment escalation plan, resuscitation decision and preferred place of care.
Which treatments or appointments create disproportionate burden.

items.title: Acute illness or injury
mustConfirmOrExclude: New physiological abnormality, delirium, focal neurological deficit, significant pain or suspected injury.
Rapid decline in mobility, transfers, oral intake, continence or ability to meet basic needs.
Medication-related harm, dehydration, acute kidney injury or other reversible deterioration.

items.title: Unsafe care environment
mustConfirmOrExclude: Carer breakdown, absent essential support, unsafe accommodation or inability to access food, fluids, medication or toileting.
Safeguarding concern, neglect, coercion or unexplained injury.
Possible end-of-life deterioration without an agreed plan or adequate symptom control.

items.title: Baseline comparison
howToTest: Use patient and collateral history to define usual cognition, mobility, self-care and support before the current deterioration.
Document the date or period representing baseline.
normal: Current state matches the established baseline.
abnormal: New cognitive, functional or care need.
implications: A new change requires an acute diagnostic assessment before it is attributed to frailty.

items.title: Observed function
howToTest: Observe transfers, standing, walking, turning and usual-aid use where safe.
Assess ability to toilet, eat, drink and manage medicines.
normal: Function matches baseline with usual support.
abnormal: New assistance or equipment requirement, unsafe gait or inability to meet essential needs.
implications: Translate findings into a specific rehabilitation, equipment or care plan.

items.title: Cognition and mood
howToTest: Screen for delirium with the 4AT when acute change is suspected.
Assess chronic cognition and mood only after considering delirium and communication barriers.
normal: Cognition and mood at baseline without acute fluctuation.
abnormal: Acute inattention, altered alertness, persistent cognitive impairment, low mood or anxiety affecting care.
implications: Arrange appropriate medical, cognitive or mental-health follow-up.

items.title: Acute illness superimposed on frailty
mustConfirmOrExclude: A new medical problem is producing disproportionate functional or cognitive decline against a vulnerable baseline.

items.title: Multidomain deterioration
mustConfirmOrExclude: Problems span medical, functional, cognitive, medicines, social or environmental domains and cannot be addressed safely as a single isolated issue.

items.title: Stable but complex needs
mustConfirmOrExclude: No immediate emergency is identified, but coordinated multidisciplinary review is required to reduce risk and treatment burden.

items.title: Create a prioritised problem list
mustConfirmOrExclude: Immediate acute problems and safety risks.
Reversible contributors to decline.
Long-term conditions and symptoms requiring optimisation.
Functional, psychological, social and environmental barriers.
Patient-defined goals and treatment limits.

items.title: Assign ownership and timescales
mustConfirmOrExclude: Named clinician or team for each action.
Urgent actions, short-term review and longer-term goals.
Communication with primary care, community services, pharmacy, therapy, social care and carers.
What should happen if the plan fails or the person deteriorates.

items.title: Reduce burden and duplication
mustConfirmOrExclude: Unnecessary medicines, investigations, appointments or conflicting plans.
Single shared care plan where possible.
Information accessible to the patient, carers and relevant services.

items.title: Record explicitly
mustConfirmOrExclude: Baseline date and source of collateral history.
Findings within each CGA domain.
Prioritised problem list and patient-defined goals.
Capacity and advance-care information.
Named action owners, timescales and review arrangements.
How the plan was shared and who has accepted responsibility.

items.title: CGA and frailty deterioration
safetyNetting: Any significant deterioration in breathing, chest pain or collapse – call 999.

Seek urgent reassessment for new confusion, a fall or injury, inability to stand or transfer, inability to eat or drink, inability to take essential medicines, reduced urine output or breakdown of the agreed care arrangement.
